results.text: M_{50,1/25} ≥ 4.0012466 on Polymath8b's epsilon-enlarged simplex, even power sums of degree 25 (1780 coefficients). With the Lean tuple (50, 246), Bombieri-Vinogradov and Polymath8b Thm 3.12(i) this gives H1 ≤ 246 end to end, the established bound. Agrees with Polymath8b's 4.00124 at degree 25 to every printed digit. Reproduction, not new.

results.label: Computed
results.text: Proposition 19 (floating point, discretised, not rigorous): the best dual weight depending only on (t_m, S), found as a convex program, is the classical k/(k-1) log k at eps = 0 and about 4.14 at (k, eps) = (50, 1/25), far above M_{50,1/25} ≥ 4.0012. Sharper floors need weights that see more of t.

results.label: Proved here
results.text: Proposition 14: M_{k,eps} ≤ (1+eps) M_k, and M_{k,eps} ≥ (1+eps) M_k − 64k²eps²/M_k for small eps, so the enlargement gains exactly (1+eps) to first order. Possibly folklore.

results.label: Proved here
results.text: Theorem 15 (floor of the epsilon-enlarged simplex): M_{k,eps} < 3.99 for every k ≤ 29 and every 0 ≤ eps < 1, so the enlarged simplex alone cannot give DHL[k,2] for k ≤ 29 from Bombieri-Vinogradov or any level θ ≤ 0.501. Inequality proved; numerical part Computed in interval arithmetic and re-checked with a second library.

results.text: With all symmetric polynomials (new generating-function formula): M_105 ≥ 4.17427, M_64 ≥ 4.00363 (degree 12); even power sums: M_58 ≥ 4.00927 (degree 16), M_56 ≥ 4.00519 (degree 18). M_55 reaches only 3.99153 at degree 18.

results.label: Proved here
results.text: Exponential-moment formula: integrals of (1-P1)^A times products of power sums over the simplex are A!/(k+A+w)! times E[prod P_j(X)^b_j] for iid Exp(1) variables, an integer given by an EGF power (Lemma 3). Possibly folklore.

results.label: Proved here
results.text: Pigeonhole rigidity also holds on Polymath8b's epsilon-enlarged simplex (Proposition 10): weights never beat the best sub-tuple. Possibly folklore.

ideas.idea: Optimise Lemma 13 over ALL weights psi_m = Psi(S - t_m, t_m) (the family containing Cor. 6.4 and the two-zone weight) as a convex program, to learn the limit of this family.
ideas.note: Discretised optimum ≈ 4.14 at (k, eps) = (50, 1/25) vs truth ≥ 4.0012; equals k/(k-1) log k at eps = 0. The family cannot reach the true threshold; need weights seeing more of t (Proposition 19).

ideas.idea: Degree extrapolation of certified M_{k,eps}: does the eps-enlarged simplex reach k = 49?
ideas.note: Geometric model validated at k = 50 (optimistic by ≤ 0.0012) predicts sup_eps M_{49,eps} ≈ 3.993 < 4: heuristic evidence that the method stops at 50 (Remark 20).

ideas.idea: Collatz-Wielandt weights psi_m = (int F dt_m)/F from a positive approximate extremal F, to approach the true floor near k = 50.
ideas.note: Exact for the extremal F; the obstacle is controlling sup over t of the ratio for a polynomial F.

ideas.idea: Active-count-normalised weight (beta/n)(a − S_A + n t_m) to beat scaling at small eps.
ideas.note: Exact fiber evaluation at k = 50, eps = 1/25: never below 4.178, worse than the scaling bound 4.1515 (Remark 18).

ideas.idea: Two-zone dual weight (linear in t_m below s1, proportional to t_m/S above) in Polymath8b's Lemma 6.1 with the marginal region kept, to bound M_{k,eps} uniformly in eps.
ideas.note: Theorem 15: no k ≤ 29 for any eps < 1, beating the k ≤ 23 floor from Polymath8b Prop. 6.5.

ideas.idea: Exponential-moment generating function for simplex integrals of power-sum products, to make certified high-degree computations cheap.
ideas.note: Lemma 3. Builds a 471x471 exact Gram pair in about 15 s.

ideas.idea: Weighted pigeonhole: give the shifts unequal weights to force two primes closer than the tuple's diameter.
ideas.note: Convexity plus perfection of unit interval graphs. Proved as Proposition 8; checked numerically for k = 3.

ideas.idea: Floor of the method: a rigorous upper bound (dual certificate) for the 2026 hybrid sieve supports, to learn how far below 186 the present inputs can go.
ideas.note: Done for the eps-enlarged simplex down to k ≤ 29 (Theorem 15). Session 4: (t_m,S)-weights stall near 4.14 at k=50 (Prop. 19); extrapolation suggests the true floor is k = 50 (Remark 20). Hybrid 2026 supports still open.

ideas.idea: Does the slicing lemma behind Proposition 8 survive on enlarged supports?
ideas.note: Yes: a single rescaling by (1+eps-|u|)/(1+eps) keeps each slice inside the eps-problem's J-region. Proposition 10; checked numerically for k = 3 and eps up to 1/3.

ideas.idea: Richer symmetric test functions to pass k = 102 and reach M_54 > 4 (270).
ideas.note: M_54 ≥ 4.0023860 at degree 23 (1236 coefficients): 270 reproduced. Next rung needs the enlarged simplex.

ideas.idea: One explicit bilinear hypothesis that implies twin primes, formalised in Lean.
ideas.note: Track B. Start from Bombieri's asymptotic sieve and Heath-Brown's Siegel-zero theorem.
